description: The practical work of keeping people's computers and networks running: the role of IT support, a disciplined troubleshooting method, hardware faults, operating-system and software problems, network connectivity issues, managing users, accounts and printers, and the documentation and customer care that make support effective. Practised on simulated machines and networks in the browser where faults are injected and resolved, mirroring the realities of shared computers, internet cafes and frequent power cuts.
modelledOn: Meyers, CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide
outcomes: Describe the role of IT support and the service desk and how tickets flow and escalate.
Apply a structured troubleshooting method to isolate and resolve a fault.
Diagnose and remedy common hardware faults and power problems.
Resolve operating-system and application issues including boot, update and malware problems.
Diagnose network connectivity problems from the device to the internet.
Manage users, accounts and printers and document work with clear customer care.

units.title: The role of IT support
topics: What IT support does: keeping people productive, not just fixing machines
The service desk, tiers of support, escalation and service-level expectations
Ticketing: logging, categorising, prioritising and tracking a request to closure
Support contexts in Ghana: schools, small businesses, internet cafes and shared computers
Professionalism, confidentiality and safety around electricity and equipment

units.title: The troubleshooting method
topics: A structured approach: identify the problem, form a theory, test, plan, implement, verify, document
Gathering information: questioning the user and reproducing the fault
Isolating a cause by halving the problem and changing one thing at a time
Distinguishing symptoms from root causes; avoiding assumptions
Knowing when to escalate and how to hand over cleanly

units.title: Hardware faults
topics: Inside the PC: power supply, motherboard, CPU, memory, storage and peripherals
Diagnosing no-power, no-boot and POST beep and error codes
Storage faults: failing drives, bad sectors, backups and data recovery basics
Overheating, dust and the effect of a hot, dusty climate on hardware
Power problems: surges, brown-outs, outages, surge protectors and the uninterruptible power supply
Safe handling, electrostatic discharge and basic component replacement

units.title: Operating system and software issues
topics: The boot process and repairing a machine that will not start
Updates, drivers and compatibility problems; rolling back a bad change
Slow or unstable systems: resources, startup programs and disk space
Malware symptoms, removal and the special risk of shared cafe machines
Backups, restore points and reinstalling an operating system as a last resort
Licensing and keeping software legal and patched

units.title: Network connectivity problems
topics: The path from a device to the internet: adapter, cable or Wi-Fi, router, ISP and beyond
IP addressing, DHCP, DNS and the gateway; reading a device's network configuration
Troubleshooting tools: ping, traceroute, nslookup and interpreting their output
Wi-Fi problems: signal, channels, interference and authentication
Diagnosing a dead link versus slow or intermittent service on shared or metered connections
When the fault is upstream: the ISP, a mobile-data outage or a cut submarine cable

units.title: Users, accounts and permissions
topics: User accounts, groups and the principle of least privilege
Password resets, account lockouts and safe identity verification of the requester
File and folder permissions and shared-resource access
Directory services and centrally managed accounts in an organisation
Onboarding and offboarding a user securely

units.title: Printers and peripherals
topics: Printer types and the print path: driver, spooler, queue and device
Diagnosing jobs that will not print, jams, quality problems and connectivity
Shared and networked printers and managing a print queue
Consumables, maintenance and cost control in a resource-constrained office

units.title: Documentation and customer care
topics: Writing clear ticket notes, resolutions and a knowledge-base article others can reuse
Asset inventories, configuration records and standard operating procedures
Communicating with non-technical users: listening, managing expectations and following up
Handling difficult situations, data loss and bad news professionally
Preventive maintenance and user training to reduce repeat problems
Capstone: work a queue of simulated tickets from logging to documented resolution

schedule.title: The support role, service desk and ticketing
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page description of how a ticket moves from a user call at a school computer lab to closure, naming each support tier and what each one may do.

tasks.title: Log, categorise and prioritise five incoming tickets from a school computer lab in a scenario, and record the priority reason for each
Route ten tickets across tier 1, tier 2 and tier 3 in a scenario, escalating only when needed and meeting the stated response times
Handle a case where a user asks for access to a colleague's files while a loose power cable is live, balancing confidentiality, safety and service levels

schedule.title: Structured troubleshooting method
schedule.exercise: Pick a fault you have met (for example no internet in a lab) and write it up as seven method steps, with the evidence for each step and what you would escalate.

tasks.title: Order the seven troubleshooting steps for a printer fault in a scenario, picking the right action at each step
Question a user in a branching case to reproduce a slow computer fault, choosing questions that separate hardware, software and user causes
Isolate a fault in a lab with six symptoms by halving the problem and changing one thing at a time, scoring fewest steps and a clean escalation

schedule.title: PC hardware faults and diagnosis
schedule.exercise: Make a fault-finding flowchart for a PC that will not start, covering power, POST beeps, memory and storage, and test it on two example faults.

tasks.title: Assemble a PC from a supplied parts list in the bench simulator and boot it successfully by connecting power, memory, storage and CPU correctly
Diagnose three PCs that do not boot from their beep codes and symptoms, and fix each by reseating or replacing the faulty part
Recover data from a PC with a failing drive in the bench simulator, deciding on cloning, backups and replacement, and verify the files are intact

schedule.title: Heat, power and safe repair
schedule.exercise: Review a computer lab in a dusty, hot town and write a maintenance plan covering cleaning intervals, UPS sizing for 10 PCs, surge protection and ESD handling.

tasks.title: Replace a RAM module in the bench simulator while following the ESD steps in the correct order
Diagnose an overheating PC in the simulator from temperature readings, find the blocked fan and dusty heatsink, and verify the temperatures drop
Size a UPS for ten PCs and a router to carry a 30-minute outage from power draws, efficiency and battery capacity, and state the cost in cedis

schedule.title: Boot repair, updates and slow systems
schedule.exercise: Write a short checklist for repairing a PC stuck in a boot loop after an update, with the safest order of actions and what data to protect first.

tasks.title: Find the process and the startup program that are using most CPU and memory on a slow virtual machine, and stop them
Roll back a bad driver or update that broke a virtual machine, verify the system works, and document each step
Repair a virtual machine that fails to boot after a damaged boot configuration, restoring service without losing user data

schedule.title: Malware, backups and licensing
schedule.exercise: Prepare a security and licensing guide for a shared internet cafe: malware signs, cleaning steps, backup routine and how to stay legally licensed on a tight budget.

tasks.title: Identify the signs of malware in six symptom reports in a scenario and choose the right first response for each
Restore a virtual machine from a restore point after a failed clean-up, then verify that user documents are intact
Clean an infected shared cafe computer in a branching case, deciding between cleaning and reinstalling, protecting customers' data and documenting the outcome

schedule.title: Network path and addressing
schedule.exercise: Draw the path from a laptop to a website, listing each device, address and protocol, and write down what you would check at each hop.

tasks.title: Read a laptop's IP address, mask, gateway and DNS server from its network configuration and state whether each is valid
Use ping and traceroute to find which hop is failing between a lab computer and an external server, and report the likely cause
Fix a lab where half the computers have the wrong address or gateway from a faulty DHCP scope, then verify all hosts reach the internet

schedule.title: Wi-Fi and upstream faults
schedule.exercise: Write a short troubleshooting guide that tells a lab assistant how to tell a dead link, a slow link and an upstream outage apart, using three quick tests.

tasks.title: Change the Wi-Fi channel of an access point to reduce interference from two neighbouring networks, and compare the signal quality before and after
Diagnose slow service on a shared metered link by finding the host using most bandwidth, and apply a limit to restore fair use
Handle an outage in a branching case where the ISP reports a submarine cable cut, choosing communication, workaround and escalation steps for a business

schedule.title: Accounts, passwords and permissions
schedule.exercise: Write a verification script for password-reset requests (who asks, what you check, what you refuse), and give one example where you would say no.

tasks.title: Create two users and a group on a Linux virtual machine, add them to the group, and show their group membership
Set file permissions so a team can read and write a shared folder while others cannot, then test access as three different users
Respond to a password-reset call from a caller who may be an impostor in a branching case, applying identity checks and handling the lockout correctly

schedule.title: Directory services, onboarding and offboarding
schedule.exercise: Draft an onboarding and offboarding checklist for a new clinic accountant, covering accounts, groups, devices, access removal and hand-over of data.

tasks.title: Create a user in Active Directory on a Windows Server virtual machine and put it in the correct organisational unit
Onboard a new employee in Active Directory with the right groups and a first-login password change, then verify what the account can reach
Offboard a leaving employee on a Windows Server by disabling the account, removing group access, and transferring the files, then audit the result

schedule.title: Printers and the print path
schedule.exercise: Create a printer troubleshooting poster that covers the print path (driver, spooler, queue, device) with the first three checks for each symptom.

tasks.title: Clear a stuck print queue and restart the print spooler service on a Windows virtual machine, and check the next job prints
Diagnose six print faults (no output, jam, streaks, offline, wrong driver and slow job) in a scenario and choose the correct fix for each
Set up a shared network printer on a server for two departments and fix the one client that cannot print, using permissions and the queue

schedule.title: Documentation and communicating with users
schedule.exercise: Write a knowledge-base article for one real fault you solved, with symptoms, cause, steps, verification and a user-friendly note, then have a partner follow it cold.

tasks.title: Write the notes and resolution for one solved ticket in a scenario, with symptom, cause, fix and verification, and score it on the rubric
Build an asset record and an SOP for replacing a failed lab PC in a scenario, and update the inventory for the changes
Handle an angry user whose work was lost in a branching case, listening, setting expectations and following up, and scored on communication

schedule.title: Prevention, difficult cases and capstone queue
schedule.exercise: Capstone reflection: describe how you prioritised a queue of simulated tickets, what you escalated, which fixes you documented, and what prevention step you would add.

tasks.title: Choose three preventive maintenance tasks and one user training topic that would reduce repeated tickets in a scenario with a ticket history
Handle a data loss incident in a branching case, delivering bad news professionally, recovering what is possible and recording the lessons learned
Work a queue of twelve mixed tickets from logging to documented resolution under time pressure, scoring on priority, escalation and clear notes
